title: silver-delta-insurance-integration-call-notes-2026-08-30
content:
Attendees: Marcus Rivera (SDI eng), Priya Nair (SDI product), Elena Soto (security), Avery Chen (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood infra)

Agenda:
- Quick intro + goals
- Review API/hosting options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
- Throughput/latency requirements and expected traffic patterns
- Data residency, PII handling, compliance (SOC2 / ISO / regional regs)
- Integration gotchas, auth, and certs
- Next steps / actions

High-level goal from customer:
- Replace current prototype that calls open LLM endpoints with a production-ready inference endpoint behind VPC.
- Must support PHI/PII use cases for claims triage and form autofill; want private deployment or VPC with strict KMS + audit.
- Target go-live for pilot with 3 business units in Q4 2026.

Traffic profile (customer-provided):
- Peak concurrent users: ~120 (expected peak 200 after pilot)
- Average request size: 600 tokens in, 150 tokens out (prompt heavy)
- Expected qps: 20 steady, burst to 60 for short windows (2-5min)
- SLA ask: P95 latency < 300ms for short prompts (<256 tokens); for long prompts acceptable to 600-800ms.
- Throughput cost sensitivity: high - they requested guidance on batching and quantization.

Security / compliance notes:
- Must run in company VPC with private control plane; cannot egress PII to public internet.
- KMS integration required (AWS KMS + HSM optional). Elena emphasized immutable audit logs for all inference requests (for later review) and ability to export logs to Splunk.
- Data retention: customer wants last 30 days of request metadata retained in Redwood console; payloads containing PHI must be purged immediately per their retention policy - asked if Redwood supports on-write redaction/field-level filtering (A: we have middleware hooks; need to confirm support for on-write redaction and provide recommended pattern).

Model / runtime preferences:
- They preferred smaller quantized models for cost but want quality checks: request Redwood Optimize recommendations based on their prompt set.
- Need model pinning and rollback policy for canary testing across 3 BU routes.
- Asked about model variants fallback: want automatic fallback to non-private hosted model if private capacity is exhausted - discussed routing policy options and cost tradeoffs.

Integration gotchas & technical concerns raised:
- Auth: they use OIDC for internal services; will need short-lived service tokens for Redwood API. Action: provide sample OIDC integration + token exchange flow.
- Egress/certificate: Private deployment requires mTLS between their sidecar and Redwood runtime for mutual auth; they asked who owns cert rotation. (A: customer typically owns internal certs; Redwood can accept certs or manage via integration with their CA.)
- KV/Prefix caching: For autofill flow they will benefit from KV cache to avoid repeating expensive context; need advice on cache TTL and invalidation across updates to customer data.
- Batching: question around latency tradeoffs. Recommended dynamic batching + per-route latency SLOs; Redwood to provide CPU/GPU sizing guidance for Dedicated pool to hit their P95 targets.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Redwood: produce a written integration checklist for Private/VPC deployment (includes network diagrams, port lists, mTLS steps, KMS cert flow). Owner: Avery. ETA: 2026-09-03.
- Redwood: run a quick cost/throughput sizing estimate for Dedicated capacity to support qps 60 burst (include batch settings, GPU type recommendations). Owner: Samir. ETA: 2026-09-06.
- Redwood: validate on-write redaction support and draft recommended middleware pattern (field-level redaction + hash storage) and confirm audit log retention options. Owner: Priya (coord with infra). ETA: 2026-09-08.
- Customer (Marcus): share example prompt set + representative dataset (anonymized) for Optimize analysis and model recommendation. ETA: 2026-09-02.
- Customer (Elena): provide security checklist + Splunk ingestion endpoints for logs. ETA: 2026-09-04.
- Set follow-up tech deep dive to demo Private deployment runbook and console walkthrough. Owner: Avery. Proposed date: week of 2026-09-07.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Confirm whether customer requires payload-level encryption at rest using their KMS keys (bring-your-own-key) or if envelope encryption is sufficient.
- Need to confirm retention: does Redwood console allow immediate purge of request payloads while keeping metadata for 30 days? if not, propose a design or workaround (e.g., stripping payloads at proxy level).
- Can Redwood support mTLS cert rotation automation with the customer's CA? If not, document manual steps and rotation frequency.

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Prioritize building the integration checklist doc - this will reduce back-and-forth and speed pilot.
- For sizing, start with A100 equivalent for Dedicated baseline then test smaller quantized models on V100/RTX-class for cost trade.
- Check if we have an existing Splunk log sink example in private-deployments docs (likely under shared_drives/engineering/observability). If yes, link it in the checklist.
- Remember to propose a staged rollout: 1) dev sandbox (non-PHI), 2) pilot BU (limited PHI), 3) full pilot (3 BUs) - tie to SLOs & monitoring.

Next meeting: Tech deep dive + security sync. Tentative: 2026-09-08 11:00 PT (wait for calendar invite from Marcus).
